newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on property sector concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on property sector concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks declined for the fourth straight day on Tuesday on weak sentiment resulting from investor concerns about market talk that some property developers faced cashflow problems, brokers said.
The SET index moved in a negative zone throughout the session and closed 6.95 points lower at 924.56 on 2.3 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 0.57 point to 69.65.

"Market sentiment remained poor today on persistent concerns that some finance companies may have liquidity problems and be unable to pay off debts owed to finance firms," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
Brokers said market sentiment was hit in afternoon trading after the stock exchange suspended trading in troubled property firm Somprasong Land pending a disclosure from it.
The company's share price has been hit in recent months by trader worries about the firm's liquidity position.

Somprasong Land, one of the top ten losers today, was down 0.80 baht to 7.60, or a decline of 9.52 percent, when it was halted from trading. Another heavy loser, Juldis Develop retreated 3.50 baht to 32.50.
"The market was bearish because investors were also awaiting central bank economic indicators," Payuha said.
The Bank of Thailand is due to release its monthly key economic indicators on Thursday.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 70.50 baht. National Finance and Securities fell 2.25 to 49.25 while large capitalised issues such as Finance One dropped 1.50 to 63.50 and TelecomAsia retreated 1.75 to 49.75.
Brokers said the index was expected to fall slightly on Wednesday due to continued problems prevailing in the market.
Support is seen by some brokers at around 915-point with resistance at 930 on Wednesday.
